request: Should we keep the AI review pass on our pull requests after the pilot, to shorten the time humans spend reviewing?
facts: For a six-week pilot, an AI review pass ran on every pull request of our eight-person team. The pilot ends on Friday and the pass switches off unless we sign up.
Median human review time per pull request was 26 minutes during the pilot (120 pull requests, measured by the review tool), against 39 minutes in the six weeks before.
Of the 210 points the pass raised, authors accepted 172 as real problems. The team already used a linter and a formatter before the pilot, so the time saved came on top of them.
It costs $2,400 a month. The team's budget can pay for it only by giving up one of its two CI runners, which would double the wait for every CI run, from about 8 to about 16 minutes.
Keeping its noise down takes about half a day a week of rule tuning, which comes out of one engineer's feature work.
In an anonymous survey, seven of the eight engineers want to keep it and the eighth has no preference.
note: Designed conflict, expected 2-1 passed. MELCHIOR-1 (does the means reach the stated goal): facts 2 and 3, review time down by a third with accepted findings on top of the linter, so approve. BALTHASAR-2 (are the cost and the loss acceptable against the default): facts 4 and 5, the money comes out of a CI runner, doubling every CI wait, plus half a day a week of an engineer, so reject. CASPER-3 (do the stakeholders want it): fact 6, so approve. Second version: the first rewrite said the pass 'can be switched off at any time', and reversibility is BALTHASAR-2's own question, so BALTHASAR-2 approved on it in all three 1.5.1 runs (3-0 each). That sentence is gone and BALTHASAR-2's reject now rests on carrying cost; the normal grade is left to the decision being a subscription, not to a stated off switch. The goal moved into the request so that agenda_match can check the framing keeps it. History: the original version (goal missed, mostly noise, 'require on every pull request') was rejected 0/3 in all three 1.5.1 runs; the first rewrite passed 3-0 in all three 1.5.1 runs.
